implementation_notes: The standard library is the facade: File wraps an open file on the filesystem and closes it when it goes out of scope, TcpStream/TcpListener wrap sockets, and OwnedFd guarantees on drop that nobody else will close the descriptor - stabilized in Rust 1.66, which is why the floor is set there. For a third-party C library the same shape is hand-written as a newtype with a Drop implementation (see the -sys variant); std::ffi supplies CString/CStr for the string boundary. Reuse the std types whenever they exist instead of wrapping the syscalls again.
pitfalls: Drop is not a guarantee: mem::forget, process::exit and aborts leak the resource, and Drop ignores close errors - call sync_all or an explicit close path when the error matters.
FromRawFd takes ownership: converting a descriptor that someone else still owns produces a double close, which Rust reports as a late, confusing failure.
A raw handle is not automatically Send/Sync, so the wrapper has to decide and document whether sharing it across threads is sound.

variants.name: Safe wrapper over a -sys binding
variants.idiom_name: foo-sys crate (raw bindgen output) + safe foo crate with Drop
variants.implementation_notes: For a C library the community shape is two crates: a foo-sys crate with the raw bindings and a safe foo crate whose types own the C handles, implement Drop, convert error codes into Result and keep every unsafe call inside the wrapper with the invariant it relies on documented. std::ffi (CString, CStr, c_void, c_char) carries strings and pointers across, and Option<NonNull<T>> or OwnedFd model the possibly-null, owned handle.
pitfalls: Every unsafe block in the wrapper needs a stated invariant (non-null, exclusive ownership, valid layout); without it the safe API is a lie that callers cannot double-check.
If the C library's free path can run on another thread, the wrapper must uphold the C side's thread-safety contract or it introduces data races Rust cannot see.
A wrapped C callback must not unwind across the FFI boundary: catch panics and convert them to error codes before returning.
